entry.title: [pipecat-ai] Pipecat: Public exposure of Pipecat’s development runner can allow unauthenticated bot session creation | Security Advisory for Python packages hosted at PyPI.org
entry.summary: Pipecat’s built-in development runner exposes endpoints that create bot sessions and, for the Daily transport, paid Daily rooms. These development endpoints intentionally do not authenticate callers.T
entry.content: Pipecat’s built-in development runner exposes endpoints that create bot sessions and, for the Daily transport, paid Daily rooms. These development endpoints intentionally do not authenticate callers.The runner binds to localhost by default and is designed exclusively for local development. It is not built or supported as a production server. Exploitation therefore requires an operator to deliberately make the development runner reachable from an untrusted network, such as by setting --host 0.0.0

entry.title: [jupyterlite-core] JupyterLab: Command link trust prompt in JupyterLab can trust a document other than the one clicked | Security Advisory for Python packages hosted at PyPI.org
entry.summary: DescriptionA Markdown file or a notebook output can carry a button that runs a JupyterLab command. Since 4.5.7 the first click on such a button opens a prompt naming the command, with Cancel, Run Once
entry.content: DescriptionA Markdown file or a notebook output can carry a button that runs a JupyterLab command. Since 4.5.7 the first click on such a button opens a prompt naming the command, with Cancel, Run Once and Trust. Choosing Trust runs the command and marks the document trusted, so its later buttons run without a prompt.Which document gets marked is decided when the user answers, not when they click. Both trust commands read whichever document is current at that moment: markdownviewer:trust uses tra

entry.title: [@anthropic-ai/claude-code] Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning | Security Advisory for JavaScript packages hosted at npmjs.com
entry.summary: The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using git checkout without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker
entry.content: The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using git checkout without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash. entry.summary: SummaryA Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, ResourceSerializer.$fill$ does Promise.resolve(resource._resolved
entry.content: SummaryA Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, ResourceSerializer.$fill$ does Promise.resolve(resource._resolved). If _resolved is a plain object whose .then is a QRL for an unregistered symbol, the async QRL rejects, the rejection is orphaned, and Node terminates the process via its default unhandled-rejection policy.ImpactOne unauthenticated request crashes the server. entry.content: SummaryCVE-2026-30973 (GHSA-rfx7-4xw3-gh4m) was a plain path traversal in the entry name.
